s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive skin lesions with upper respiratory tract involvement and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
Palatal perforation and stridor necessitating tracheostomy
Saddle nose deformity and destruction of ear cartilage
key_facts: Woman in her 30s
Lesions started as an erythematous papule on the face and progressed to larger plaques within 10 years
Involvement of the upper respiratory tract
History of wheezing and breathlessness
No history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
Multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring
Cervical lymphadenopathy with multiple, nontender, discrete nodes
Anemia with hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Normal kidney function test, liver function test, fasting blood glucose, and urinalysis
Negative serologic analysis for HIV-1/2, antinuclear antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
Normal chest radiography
Punch skin biopsy showing infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts
Histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes

shortlist.label: Leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic progressive skin lesions with upper respiratory tract involvement and anemia

shortlist.label: Relapsing polychondritis
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the upper respiratory tract and destruction of ear cartilage

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Upper respiratory tract involvement and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Lupus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic progressive skin lesions with scarring and upper respiratory tract involvement

shortlist.label: Chronic cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic progressive skin lesions with scarring and systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, and parakeratosis in the histopathology, along with the involvement of the upper respiratory tract and cervical lymphadenopathy, are consistent with lupus vulgaris, a form of cutaneous tuberculosis

rejected.label: Leprosy
rejected.why: Lack of sensory examination abnormalities and peripheral nerve involvement

rejected.label: Relapsing polychondritis
rejected.why: No history of preceding trauma, fever, or malaise, and absence of cartilage destruction beyond the ear

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Negative antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies and absence of renal or pulmonary involvement

rejected.label: Chronic cutaneous lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Negative antinuclear antibody and absence of characteristic discoid lupus lesions
